findings.quote: "claim": "AWS does not provide a synchronous cross-Region replication feature." (evidence quote: "AWS does not provide a synchronous Cross-Region replication feature at this time."; volatility stable, changed null)
findings.evidence: source_id full:amazondynamodb-developerguide (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/full.md, fetched 2026-10-05), line 11742: "With multi-Region strong consistency (MRSC), item changes are synchronously replicated to another Region before the write returns, and strongly consistent read operations on any replica always return the latest version of an item." Line 20452: "MRSC global tables support a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of zero." Document history, line 126185, dated June 30, 2025: "MRSC allows strongly consistent reads across Regions with a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of zero during regional failures." The whitepaper sentence ('at this time') predates this; the fact drops 'at this time' and is marked stable. GA on 2025-06-30 is more than 3 months before the exam, so by RULINGS hard rule 7 it is examinable and needs a 'Changed recently' note. Fix: amend the fact (scope it, for example 'most AWS replication features between Regions are asynchronous; DynamoDB global tables in MRSC mode replicate synchronously'), register an MRSC fact from the DynamoDB guide, and re-run the currency vote. Every dependent below must change with it.

findings.quote: "Which solution will ensure data residency with the LEAST operational overhead?" Key: "Create the S3 bucket and the EC2 instances in the Region in that country, and do not turn on any cross-Region replication or copy feature." Why: "No extra setting or job is needed."
findings.evidence: Item-writer realism: on the real exam 'ensure' asks for a control that prevents a violation, and the usual answer for Region restriction is an SCP or a Control Tower control that denies other Regions (FREQUENCY row 25, research input: 'SCPs cap permissions ... Control Tower guardrails'). The key ensures nothing: any engineer can still enable a replication or copy feature or create a bucket in another Region, and the fact the key relies on says data leaves only 'unless you explicitly use a replication or copy feature' (global-infrastructure-no-automatic-cross-region-replication). The worked example, the first question she sees, then teaches that 'ensure' means 'do nothing'. Fix: change the verb to 'keep the data in the country' or 'Which deployment meets the law', or keep 'ensure' and make the key 'deploy in that Region and add a Region-deny guardrail' with an xref to the Organizations chapter.
findings.resolution: fix-02: rejected. Among the four options the key is the only one that meets the law with the least work, and all three blind solvers agreed (pass). Changing the stem verb or the key would reset a verified worked example. Region-deny guardrails belong to chapter 04 (Organizations); logged for the next question revision.

findings.quote: "If the stem said \"the law allows any Region inside the European Union\" instead: the lowest-priced Region in the European Union, because prices are [different in each Region](...)"
findings.evidence: SPEC.json twin_rules: the twin differs by one deciding phrase. The stem's qualifier is 'LEAST operational overhead', not cost, so with the changed phrase price would not decide; any EU Region would meet the law with the same overhead. The twin silently swaps the qualifier, which trains her to ignore the qualifier, the habit READER.md says she must build ('find the constraint in the stem'). Fix: twin 'If the stem said "MOST cost-effective" and "any Region inside the European Union"' or pick a twin that keeps the qualifier.
findings.resolution: fix-02: explanation-only edit of the q008 twin: 'If the stem said "any European Union Region meets the law" and "MOST cost-effective" instead: the lowest-priced of those Regions, because prices are different in each Region.' The qualifier change is now stated.
